Priya: quick note 1 - the Python quickstart README still uses requests with the api_key in the query string and an older method name `generate_text`. New SDKs use `client.responses.create` etc. People copy this and get 401s or confused errors.

Omar: argh, which file?

Priya: docs/quickstart/python/README.md top snippet. current snippet:```python
import requests
res = requests.post('https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate?api_key=sk-XXXX', json={'input': 'hello'})
print(res.text)
```

DocBot: automated-doc-scan: SDK parity drift detected (severity: medium). Suggest replacing with requests example that uses Authorization header and also adding a minimal official SDK example.

Nina: good catch. we should also add a tiny note about not logging keys and how to set env var on Windows (setx /M) vs bash export.

Omar: I'll open a tiny PR to: 1) fix curl and python examples to use header, 2) add a one-line SDK example with `from redwood import Client
client = Client()` 3) link to auth best-practices. PR will reference issue #4780.

Priya: please include a short comment about backoff on 429s and that the sample shows a single-shot request only. new users paste stack traces without seeing they used query-string auth.
